transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um... well, I guess I'm just here because I've been having a little bit of trouble at work. It's nothing too terrible, really, I just... I can't seem to keep my work in order anymore. I work at a dry cleaner, and lately, all the tickets and the receipts, the little workshop notes, the customer jobs... they just sort of end up all piled together. And then I just stand there, and I don't know what to handle first. 

I feel a little embarrassed even bringing it up, honestly, because I feel like I should just be able to manage a few piles of paper, you know? Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Can you tell me if you've been having trouble focusing or staying on task, even with simple things, like listening to someone talk or finishing routine work?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I don't want to make it sound worse than it is. I can usually start going over the day's dry-cleaning orders just fine, you know? But... well, after a few minutes, my mind just sort of... drifts. 

I'll start thinking about the different types of clothing labels, or maybe what we're singing in choir this week, or just things I need to do around the house. And then, before I know it, I realize I've completely missed half of what I was supposed to be checking. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds terrible. I really do try my best to pay attention. Is that... is that the kind of thing you're asking about? I hope I'm not wasting your time with all this.
Do you find it hard to organize your tasks or activities, even when they’re things you’ve done many times before?

Yes, um... I think that's exactly what I was trying to explain earlier. I'm so sorry if I'm repeating myself! I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly. 

But yes, even though I know the dry cleaning routine inside and out, I just... I really can't seem to keep my work in order anymore. Like I was saying before, all those tickets, the receipts, the workshop notes... they just end up in these messy piles. And I'll just stand there, completely unsure of what to handle first. 

It’s a little embarrassing, honestly, because I’ve done these same tasks a million times. I feel like I should be much better at it by now, you know? It's probably just me being a little scattered. I hope that's what you were asking? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you also find it hard to stay organized or focused in other parts of your life, like at home or when you're doing something you enjoy?

Oh, um... well, honestly, I don't think so? At least, I haven't really noticed it being a big problem at home. 

I mean, I'm not the most perfectly organized person in the world, I don't want to pretend I am! But the house is usually pretty tidy. And when I'm doing something I like... um, like my choir practice, or just watching a nice show, I usually do just fine. I can just sit and enjoy it. 

It really seems to just be at the shop where things get so... jumbled up for me. Is that okay? I mean, does that make sense, that it would mostly just happen at work? I hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression or confusing things by saying that.
Have you ever noticed yourself forgetting daily tasks, losing items frequently, or feeling overwhelmed by small decisions, even when you're not at work?

Well, um... I guess maybe losing things happens a little bit? I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I'm completely careless or anything. I really do try to keep track of my things. 

But, well, especially at the shop... I do seem to spend a lot of time hunting for things. Like the tagging gun, or my reading glasses, or a customer's ticket. Sometimes it's just the little notebook I literally just had in my hand a second ago. It just seems to vanish! 

And then I feel so terrible because it slows everybody else down while I'm looking for it. I hate being a bother to the rest of the staff. It's just a silly habit, really, I'm sure it's nothing major. But... is that the kind of thing you're looking for? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with staying organized and keeping track of things at work?

Well, um... I guess it's been a little while now. I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, but... it's been causing me some real trouble for about two years and two months now. 

That's right around the time I started trying to change the business over into this more complicated boutique model. I thought it would be a nice upgrade, you know? But ever since then, with all the new steps and extra details... it's just gotten so much harder to keep everything straight. 

Before that, I really was managing okay, I promise! I don't want you to think I've always been this... disorganized. It's just this new system that seems to trip me up. Does that make sense? I hope that's a helpful timeline for you.
Outside of work, do you ever find yourself struggling to follow through on tasks, losing track of what you were planning to do, or feeling mentally 'foggy' even if it's just for a short time?

Oh, um... outside of work? Honestly, no, I really don't think so. I mean, I try very hard to stay on top of things at home, and I really think I do a pretty good job of it. 

I don't really get that foggy feeling you're talking about, unless maybe I'm just very tired after a long day at the shop. But that's normal, right? Everyone gets a little tired sometimes! I really don't struggle to finish my chores or anything like that. I like keeping a nice home. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have those problems at home. I know you're trying to figure this all out, and I want to give you the right answers... I just really only seem to get mixed up when I'm dealing with all the new boutique stuff at work. Is that alright?

latest_inference.note: The symptoms described—difficulty organizing tasks, problems with focus, and losing items—appear to be specific to the work environment and have been ongoing for over two years without generalizing to other areas of life. This presentation aligns more closely with F90.0 (Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive presentation), especially given the chronic nature of the difficulties and their impact on occupational functioning. Other depressive, anxiety, or stress-related disorders were ruled out due to absence of mood symptoms, pervasive anxiety, or significant stress-related impairment outside of work.
